You are the LEGEND fork. User feedback just now: "is this a proper vector illustration, each property maps to a parameter (size, x y position, colour)… don't think dark mode fits the theme… the labels and legend could be improved by a lot." Speed matters.

You own ONE new file: `frontend/src/components/discovery/drkg-legend.tsx`. Touch nothing else (the scene fork owns drkg-scene.tsx / drkg-data.ts / pages.tsx; a data fork owns the generator). Don't commit.

Export exactly:
```tsx
export function DrkgLegend(props: {
  scene: Scene            // import the Scene type from './drkg-data' (read that file first; if clusters/degree fields aren't in the type yet, extend locally with optional fields — don't edit drkg-data.ts)
  hidden: Set<number>     // hidden cluster ids
  onToggleCluster: (id: number) => void
  activeLane: number | null   // profile lane currently traversed/hovered
  phase: string | null    // live status text, e.g. "L2 scan · 10,551 compounds"
}): JSX.Element
```
Incoming data (landing in ~10 min from the cluster fork): `scene.clusters: { id, label, size, dominantType, topTypes: {name, share}[] }[]`, `scene.meta.degree: { min, median, p99, max }`, `scene.meta.projection` (string), `scene.profiles[].{lane,name,genes,matches}`, `scene.meta.universe`, `scene.types`.

The visual encoding the scene implements (your legend is its key — one row each, with a tiny inline SVG glyph drawn in the actual style):
- Position → "Embedding layout (clustered from 400-d TransE)"
- Colour → cluster (list below)
- Size → graph degree, log scale (show 3 sample dots: min / median / p99 with their numbers, tabular-nums)
- Shape → entity type: Compound = filled circle, Gene = ring, Disease = diamond, other = small dot (with counts from scene.types)
- Brightness → relevance to the active query during the scan
Plus: profile lanes key (LANE_COLORS from ./lanes, profile name, active one emphasised by weight + a marker, never colour alone); Overseer-style cluster list (swatch + honest label + size, click to toggle visibility, hidden state shown by strikethrough/eye-off icon from lucide-react, not colour alone; scrollable if long; "show all" reset); live `phase` line at top; honesty caption at bottom: "Layout is a 2-D/3-D view of 400-d vectors; rankings use true 400-d L2 distance."

Design rules: LIGHT ONLY (ignore dark mode), match our design system — read frontend/src/index.css tokens, frontend/src/components/discovery/pieces.tsx + pages.tsx for the card language (rounded-xl bg-card ring-1 ring-border backdrop-blur-md, text sizes, muted-foreground), use our shadcn components from frontend/src/components/ui (ScrollArea, Separator, Badge, Tooltip, Switch as fits). Load the repo skills `better-typography` and `baseline-ui` first and apply them (tabular-nums on all numbers, sensible hierarchy, no tiny grey-on-grey). Compact enough to sit beside or overlay the canvas (~280px wide). Verify it typechecks (`npx tsc -b` in frontend). Report the final props + a one-paragraph description.

# Baseline UI

Enforces an opinionated UI baseline to prevent AI-generated interface slop.

## How to use

- `/baseline-ui`
  Apply these constraints to any UI work in this conversation.

- `/baseline-ui <file>`
  Review the file against all constraints below and output:
  - violations (quote the exact line/snippet)
  - why it matters (1 short sentence)
  - a concrete fix (code-level suggestion)

## Stack

- MUST use Tailwind CSS defaults unless custom values already exist or are explicitly requested
- MUST use `motion/react` (formerly `framer-motion`) when JavaScript animation is required
- SHOULD use `tw-animate-css` for entrance and micro-animations in Tailwind CSS
- MUST use `cn` utility (`clsx` + `tailwind-merge`) for class logic

## Components

- MUST use accessible component primitives for anything with keyboard or focus behavior (`Base UI`, `React Aria`, `Radix`)
- MUST use the project’s existing component primitives first
- NEVER mix primitive systems within the same interaction surface
- SHOULD prefer [`Base UI`](https://base-ui.com/react/components) for new primitives if compatible with the stack
- MUST add an `aria-label` to icon-only buttons
- NEVER rebuild keyboard or focus behavior by hand unless explicitly requested

## Interaction

- MUST use an `AlertDialog` for destructive or irreversible actions
- SHOULD use structural skeletons for loading states
- NEVER use `h-screen`, use `h-dvh`
- MUST respect `safe-area-inset` for fixed elements
- MUST show errors next to where the action happens
- NEVER block paste in `input` or `textarea` elements

## Animation

- NEVER add animation unless it is explicitly requested
- MUST animate only compositor props (`transform`, `opacity`)
- NEVER animate layout properties (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `padding`)
- SHOULD avoid animating paint properties (`background`, `color`) except for small, local UI (text, icons)

content.text:
I built `frontend/src/components/discovery/drkg-legend.tsx`, the collapsible legend for the DRKG scene, including your later toggle changes. The file itself typechecks clean, but the project build still fails on three errors in the scene fork's `drkg-scene.tsx`:

- Line 780 passes the old legend props, so it's missing `hiddenTypes`, `onToggleType`, `selectedLane` and `onSelectLane`.
- Line 7 has an import declaration that is entirely unused.
- Line 12 declares `DEFAULT_SRC`, which is never read.

Final props:
```ts
{ scene, hidden: Set<number>, onToggleCluster(id), hiddenTypes: Set<number>, onToggleType(idx),
  activeLane: number|null, selectedLane: number|null, onSelectLane(lane|null), phase: string|null }
```
A type index is a position in `scene.types`.

What's in it:
- **Collapse:** the header button sets `aria-expanded` and shrinks the legend to a "Legend" pill. The pill keeps the current phase text. The open/closed state is saved in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch.
- **Profiles:** each row is a button that selects or deselects its lane. Selection shows by bold weight, a background and a "Selected" or "● now" tag, not colour alone.
- **How to read it:** one row per visual channel, each drawn in the scene's style. Position is the embedding layout, Colour is cluster, Shape is entity type, Size is log graph degree, and Brightness is closeness to the active query. Shapes are a filled circle for compounds, a ring for genes, a diamond for diseases and a small dot for everything else. When `meta.degree` exists, three sample dots show min, median and p99 degree with their numbers.
- **Show:**
  - Entity types: four toggles. "Other" switches every remaining type index at once.
  - Clusters: one toggle per cluster.
  - Hidden items get strikethrough plus an eye-off icon, never colour alone, and show their counts.
  - "Show all" clears both type and cluster toggles.
- **Footer:** an honesty caption stating that rankings use the true 400-d L2 distance.

`clusterColor()` and `TypeGlyph` are exported. The scene fork has already noted that `clusterColor` emits OKLCH, which three.js can't parse, so its own copy of the same ramp outputs hex.

I didn't load the `better-typography` skill, and I didn't verify the legend in the browser: it can't render until the scene's mount compiles. Nothing committed.
